title: MZ Pixel Fonts Are Blurred in Centered Text in Menus, Can I Fix This?

posts.author: JimFrom2003
posts.body:
I found a pixelated font for my low-resolution game, but the problem is, on certain menus (title screen, options, etc.) the text is blurred on certain lines. I think it's because they way RMMZ centers text causes it to land on half-pixels. I've tried getting the pixels to align properly by writing a plugin and using math.Round(), but nothing seems to work. Does anyone have any idea which variables I should try tweaking or if there's a different method I should try, or is it just another hard-coded "quirk" of RPG Maker that I'm just going to have to work around?
Here's an image of what's going on in case visual aid is necessary. Note how "New Game" and "Continue" are nice and crisp while "Options" is blurred a little.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Judging by my notes, I've used this to fix a similar problem in my project:
JavaScript:
/*:
 * @target MZ
 * @plugindesc Render at integer coordinates.
 * @url https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/172982/
 */
PIXI.settings.ROUND_PIXELS = true;

posts.body:

Click to expand...
This doesn't seem to work for me.
Closest I've gotten to a solution is nudging the x-coordinate for where the text renders half a pixel to the side. This unblurs the previously affected text, but the rest of the text is blurred.
I also forgot to mention that since I'm making a low-resolution game, I scaled down the text boxes by about half to fit. Do you think that affected it in any way? I might have, as RPG Maker, quite ironically, is weirdly hostile to low-res games.

Still doesn't work. "Options" is still blurry.
Like, I've said, Math.round() doesn't seem to be working for getting the text aligned for some reason. I don't know what to do.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Drat. From what I've gathered, font rendering seems to be a fairly intractable source of anti-aliasing, at least in web development. There are workarounds, though!
Scaling down the text's texture may well cause blurriness; by default a window's contents is set to linear scaling ("smooth") rather than nearest-neighbour. If you want to remove all graphical anti-aliasing, you could try a plugin like this:
Pixel Perfect for RPG Maker MV/MZ by Galenmereth
A free pay-if-you-want plugin for RPG Maker MV and MZ that enables pixel-perfect scaling mode
galenmereth.itch.io
For the font stuff specifically, maybe check out one of these:
Eli Bitmap Font - bitmap fonts are probably best if you want total graphical fidelity.
Eli Bitmap Font - Use bitmap fonts into your game!
Author: Hakuen Studio  Introduction  Those who want to use pixel fonts, or even more detailed fonts can get into a lot of trouble when aiming for the perfection of the font visuals. Rpg Maker can blur and add an outline to your fonts. This plugin solves this problem, letting you use a bitmap...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
OpenType Pixel Font Renderer by utunnels - custom TrueType parser, see this post for MZ:
MZ - OpenType Pixel Font Renderer (MV & MZ)
Download link: https://utstudio.itch.io/otpfmvz  Introduction This plugin uses opentype.js - an OpenType/TTF font parser - to achieve precise text rendering in both browser and Node.js environments. The plugin is designed specifically for pixel-perfect font display, it modifies the core...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Sharp Text by MechPen - this one seems to manually "fix" font edges on a per-pixel basis?
Sharp Text [MZ + MV]
utunnels was able to solve this with a plugin utilizing opentype.js Go and use that one. The Sharp Text plugin will still be maintained for people who are using it but I highly recommend OpenType Pixel Font Renderer instead.  Sharp Text v0.94 beta MechPen  Introduction I'm working on a...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
I'm glad that you find it useful.
To be fair, every method requires the font itself to be accurate. My plugin also do Math.round but on every corner of the glyphs. I also found certain characters became deformed while other characters from the same font looked OK.
If that happens, you'll need to find a good font or use fontforge to fix those characters.
